sections.history: Patteeswaram is an old Shaiva village in the fertile Kaveri delta south-west of Kumbakonam, and its temple is a Paadal Petra Sthalam praised in the hymns of Thirugnana Sambandar. The town takes its name from Patti, the calf of the divine cow Kamadhenu, whose worship of the Lord here is remembered in the sthala purana. Enlarged in stone under the Cholas and their successors, the temple grew into a substantial complex with a tall gopuram and spacious courtyards. It is counted among the temples associated with the Kumbakonam Mahamaham cluster and has remained a living centre of Shiva and Devi worship through the centuries.
sections.architecture: The temple is entered through a towering gopuram and spreads across broad prakara courtyards in the Dravidian manner. The sanctum houses the Shiva linga of Dhenupureeswarar, with the goddess Gnanambikai in her own shrine. The temple is above all celebrated for its shrine of Durga, where the goddess stands in a graceful eight-armed form, flanked by guardians, and is worshipped as one of the most beautiful Durga images of the delta. Pillared halls, a temple tank, and sculpted mandapams complete the complex.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Kamadhenu, the celestial wish-granting cow, had daughters, and that her calf Patti came to this place to worship Shiva. Fashioning a linga of sand on the bank, Patti bathed it in her own milk, and the Lord accepted that devotion and stayed in the linga; from Patti the village became Patteeswaram and the Lord Patteeswarar, also Dhenupureeswarar, the Lord of the cow's town. Tradition also holds that Parvati did penance here, served by Patti, before her union with Shiva.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri, the Tamil month festivals, and the Durga-centred observances of the Navaratri season are kept with special fervour, given the fame of the standing Durga shrine. The monthly Pradosham and the car festival draw devotees from across the delta, and the Kumbakonam Mahamaham cycle is observed. Festival dates follow the Tamil calendar, so confirm them locally.
sections.experience: Pilgrims come to Patteeswaram as much for the goddess as for the Lord: many enter first to the celebrated standing Durga, then worship Dhenupureeswarar and Gnanambikai in the main shrines. The temple keeps the unhurried air of a delta village sanctuary, close to Kumbakonam and Swamimalai, and is often included in a day of temple visits around the Mahamaham town.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Patteeswaram lies about 9 km south-west of Kumbakonam and about 3 km south-east of Swamimalai in Thanjavur district. Kumbakonam is the nearest major railway station; Tiruchirappalli airport is about 90 km away. Local buses and autos run from Kumbakonam.
